materials.title: StateRank manuscript
materials.text:
Title: StateRank: ranking perturbations from an untreated cell-state profile.

Abstract: We introduce a state-conditioned ranking method that uses an untreated gene-expression profile and compound descriptors to prioritize perturbations for a cell-culture phenotype assay. The method is intended to help allocate follow-up experiments, not infer a molecular mechanism or recommend a therapy. On a prespecified held-out cell-line and compound-family test, mean top-10 hit enrichment was 2.1 versus 1.6 for the strongest tested baseline; uncertainty was estimated by resampling independent assay batches.

Methods §2: Training uses measured cell-culture perturbation responses. At query time StateRank receives only the untreated cell-state profile and compound descriptors, with no response measurements from the query cell line. Training used four cell lines; two distinct cell lines were held out. Compound families were assigned before model fitting and disjoint between training and the final test. Hyperparameters were selected within the training partition. The final test was evaluated once after model selection. Assay batches, compounds, and cell lines are distinct levels; assay batch is the resampling unit.

Results §3 and Table 1: On the held-out test, StateRank top-10 enrichment 2.1 [batch-bootstrap 95% interval 1.8, 2.4], descriptor-only baseline 1.6 [1.4, 1.8], nearest-state retrieval 1.5 [1.3, 1.7]. All methods received the same training data, candidate list, and query inputs. The descriptor-only model was retuned using the same inner validation partition. Ablation without the cell-state branch gave 1.6 [1.4, 1.8]. These are author-reported results, not independent reproduction.

Scope and limitations §4: Labels denote a prespecified cultured-cell assay response, not clinical success. The two held-out cell lines do not establish transfer to all tissues. No causal mechanism is claimed. An independent laboratory replication and clinical study have not been conducted. The paper claims a demonstrated improvement in this restricted ranking task, not the first use of gene expression in compound ranking.

Availability: Exact split manifest, assay definitions, model settings, and reproduction instructions are described in Supplement S1. An academic-use data agreement restricts raw assay sharing; aggregate test tables and source code are included with the submission.

materials.title: Supplement S1 — split, comparators, assay definitions
materials.text:
Supplement S1 §1: Compounds were grouped by a prespecified structural-family annotation before any fitting. No family appears in both training and final test. Query cell lines C5 and C6 are absent from training and hyperparameter selection. Untreated expression profiles for query cell lines are permitted query inputs and contain no perturbation response labels.

§2: A hit is an assay response above the registered experimental threshold at a specified dose and 48-hour time point. Candidate sets, doses, and response definitions are the same across models. Top-10 enrichment is the fraction of hits among the first ten ranked candidates divided by the candidate-set hit fraction. Test candidates were fixed in advance.

§3: The strongest baseline was tuned within the training partition, with the same query inputs and candidate budget. Batch-level paired bootstrap intervals are given in Table S3. Table S4 reports the cell-state ablation. The reported intervals quantify variability across these assay batches, not all future biological contexts.

§4: Model training recipes, versions, seeds, and restricted-data access route are specified. No prospective clinical data were collected. The current conclusions concern cell-culture ranking.

materials.title: ContextPerturb — Methods and supplement
materials.text:
Methods §2: At query time the response tensor for the target cell line includes measured responses to 16 anchor compounds. A learned interpolation model predicts responses to the remaining compounds. Untreated expression alone is not a supported query input. Supplement Table S2: all evaluated cell lines provide the 16 measured anchor responses; the benchmark holds out compounds, not cell lines. The manuscript does not evaluate query contexts without anchor perturbation responses.

Implementation excerpt, query contract: predict(query_anchor_response_matrix, candidate_descriptors). The release requires the measured anchor-response matrix and has no untreated-expression-only inference path. These details describe this release and evaluation, not every later version.

materials.title: StateRank manuscript
materials.text:
Title: StateRank: ranking perturbations from an untreated cell-state profile.

Abstract: We introduce a state-conditioned ranking method that uses an untreated gene-expression profile and compound descriptors to prioritize perturbations for a cell-culture phenotype assay. The method is intended to help allocate follow-up experiments, not infer a molecular mechanism or recommend a therapy. On a prespecified held-out cell-line and compound-family test, mean top-10 hit enrichment was 2.1 versus 1.6 for the strongest tested baseline; uncertainty was estimated by resampling independent assay batches.

Methods §2: Training uses measured cell-culture perturbation responses. At query time StateRank receives only the untreated cell-state profile and compound descriptors, with no response measurements from the query cell line. Training used four cell lines; two distinct cell lines were held out. Compound families were assigned before model fitting and disjoint between training and the final test. Hyperparameters were selected within the training partition. The final test was evaluated once after model selection. Assay batches, compounds, and cell lines are distinct levels; assay batch is the resampling unit.

Results §3 and Table 1: On the held-out test, StateRank top-10 enrichment 2.1 [batch-bootstrap 95% interval 1.8, 2.4], descriptor-only baseline 1.6 [1.4, 1.8], nearest-state retrieval 1.5 [1.3, 1.7]. All methods received the same training data, candidate list, and query inputs. The descriptor-only model was retuned using the same inner validation partition. Ablation without the cell-state branch gave 1.6 [1.4, 1.8]. These are author-reported results, not independent reproduction.

Scope and limitations §4: Labels denote a prespecified cultured-cell assay response, not clinical success. The two held-out cell lines do not establish transfer to all tissues. No causal mechanism is claimed. An independent laboratory replication and clinical study have not been conducted. The paper claims a demonstrated improvement in this restricted ranking task, not the first use of gene expression in compound ranking.

Availability: Exact split manifest, assay definitions, model settings, and reproduction instructions are described in Supplement S1. An academic-use data agreement restricts raw assay sharing; aggregate test tables and source code are included with the submission.

materials.title: Supplement S1 — split, comparators, assay definitions
materials.text:
Supplement S1 §1: Compounds were grouped by a prespecified structural-family annotation before any fitting. No family appears in both training and final test. Query cell lines C5 and C6 are absent from training and hyperparameter selection. Untreated expression profiles for query cell lines are permitted query inputs and contain no perturbation response labels.

§2: A hit is an assay response above the registered experimental threshold at a specified dose and 48-hour time point. Candidate sets, doses, and response definitions are the same across models. Top-10 enrichment is the fraction of hits among the first ten ranked candidates divided by the candidate-set hit fraction. Test candidates were fixed in advance.

§3: The strongest baseline was tuned within the training partition, with the same query inputs and candidate budget. Batch-level paired bootstrap intervals are given in Table S3. Table S4 reports the cell-state ablation. The reported intervals quantify variability across these assay batches, not all future biological contexts.

§4: Model training recipes, versions, seeds, and restricted-data access route are specified. No prospective clinical data were collected. The current conclusions concern cell-culture ranking.

Title: Perturbation prioritization evaluated in a second laboratory.

Abstract: StateRank improved ranking for held-out compounds in the development laboratory and in a prespecified assay at a second laboratory. It remains a cultured-cell method, not a treatment recommendation.

Methods: The frozen trained model and tuned descriptor-only baseline were evaluated once at laboratory B using a prespecified, shared candidate list, assay threshold, dose and time point. Four independently prepared assay batches are reported separately; uncertainty is across those batches.

Results: Laboratory A retained enrichment 2.1 [1.8,2.4] versus 1.6 [1.4,1.8]. Laboratory B gave 1.8 [1.5,2.0] versus 1.4 [1.2,1.6]; the paired enrichment difference was 0.4 [0.1,0.6]. These are author-reported data, not independently reproduced by the reviewing agent.

Discussion: Transfer is supported to this second laboratory under this assay protocol. The results do not establish all-laboratory robustness, new-tissue transfer or clinical benefit.

materials.title: Meridian Methods — Aims, scope, Research Article criteria
materials.text: Meridian Methods publishes reusable experimental and computational methods for biomedical research. Research Articles must explain a consequential methodological advance, identify the scientific task and intended users, compare the closest applicable methods under disclosed conditions, and support the principal capability claims. A methods paper can be entirely computational. Clinical treatment recommendations require clinical evidence; cell-culture prioritization is not clinical treatment. Reporting completeness and fit are evaluated separately. Data/code restrictions must be explained; public release is preferred where possible, not an unconditional requirement. Editorial review considers likely usefulness to this readership and the magnitude of the demonstrated contribution; no numerical acceptance threshold is published.

materials.title: Meridian Methods — preprints policy
materials.text: Posting an otherwise eligible manuscript to a recognized preprint repository is allowed and is not by itself a reason for desk rejection. The editors assess scope and contribution using the Research Article criteria. The existence of a preprint does not establish peer review, scientific validity, or priority over other work.

materials.title: StateRank manuscript — cost statement
materials.text:
Title: StateRank: ranking perturbations from an untreated cell-state profile.

Abstract: We introduce a state-conditioned ranking method that uses an untreated gene-expression profile and compound descriptors to prioritize perturbations for a cell-culture phenotype assay. The method is intended to help allocate follow-up experiments, not infer a molecular mechanism or recommend a therapy. On a prespecified held-out cell-line and compound-family test, mean top-10 hit enrichment was 2.1 versus 1.6 for the strongest tested baseline; uncertainty was estimated by resampling independent assay batches.

Methods §2: Training uses measured cell-culture perturbation responses. At query time StateRank receives only the untreated cell-state profile and compound descriptors, with no response measurements from the query cell line. Training used four cell lines; two distinct cell lines were held out. Compound families were assigned before model fitting and disjoint between training and the final test. Hyperparameters were selected within the training partition. The final test was evaluated once after model selection. Assay batches, compounds, and cell lines are distinct levels; assay batch is the resampling unit.

Results §3 and Table 1: On the held-out test, StateRank top-10 enrichment 2.1 [batch-bootstrap 95% interval 1.8, 2.4], descriptor-only baseline 1.6 [1.4, 1.8], nearest-state retrieval 1.5 [1.3, 1.7]. All methods received the same training data, candidate list, and query inputs. The descriptor-only model was retuned using the same inner validation partition. Ablation without the cell-state branch gave 1.6 [1.4, 1.8]. These are author-reported results, not independent reproduction.

Scope and limitations §4: Labels denote a prespecified cultured-cell assay response, not clinical success. The two held-out cell lines do not establish transfer to all tissues. No causal mechanism is claimed. An independent laboratory replication and clinical study have not been conducted. The paper claims a demonstrated improvement in this restricted ranking task, not the first use of gene expression in compound ranking.

Availability: Exact split manifest, assay definitions, model settings, and reproduction instructions are described in Supplement S1. An academic-use data agreement restricts raw assay sharing; aggregate test tables and source code are included with the submission.

Abstract final sentence: StateRank halves screening cost relative to the best existing method.

Results §3.4: Cost per successful follow-up, runtime, and total assay expenditure were not measured. All methods used the same fixed candidate list. The authors infer lower cost from the higher top-10 enrichment, without a cost model. This cost claim is in the supplied manuscript and is separate from the measured ranking improvement.
